name: adv_ppo_clean
title: PPO with a rollout buffer, GAE, a clipped objective and an entropy bonus - correct
origin: written for the domain-generative-rl-graph hardening round, 2026-09-13
note: A correct on-policy RL trainer. Every row here is `forbidden`: this program exists to prove that the torch rule set stays silent on a hand-written minibatch update, on a rollout loop that deliberately does not switch to eval mode, and on an evaluation helper that does.

forbidden.why: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is called at line 148, at the top of every minibatch step, before the backward pass
optimizer.step() is called at line 151, after loss.backward() at line 149
the order in the minibatch block is zero_grad (148) -> backward (149) -> clip (150) -> step (151)
the only no_grad blocks are the rollout forward (line 91) and the bootstrap value (line 194); loss.backward() at line 149 is outside both
total_loss accumulates loss.item() at line 152, not the live tensor
evaluate_policy() calls policy.eval() at line 158 and restores policy.train() at line 173; collect_rollout() is part of the training loop and correctly stays in train mode
evaluate_policy() wraps its whole episode loop in torch.no_grad() at line 160, and the rollout forward is inside torch.no_grad() at line 91
no softmax is applied anywhere: the policy head returns logits straight into Categorical(logits=...), and the value loss is F.mse_loss
there is no binary cross-entropy of any kind in this project
every observation is built with torch.as_tensor(..., device=DEVICE) and the buffer allocates on the same device
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 25
random.seed, np.random.seed and torch.manual_seed are all called at lines 178-180
there is no train/test split call in this project at all - the data is generated by the environment
ActorCritic.__init__ calls super().__init__() on its first line (line 40)
policy_head and value_head are plain attributes, so nn.Module registers both; no list or dict of submodules exists
torch.save is given policy.state_dict() at line 205, not the module
